title: Localized Cultural Knowledge is Conserved and Controllable in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model accuracy on a Cultural Localization Benchmark (covering names, cities, and local customs) by comparing responses to implicit prompts (language only) versus explicit prompts (explicitly stated cultural context), and using an LLM-as-a-judge to measure stereotypicality and cultural faithfulness in open-ended generations.

Measuring the 'explicit-implicit localization gap' by analyzing whether large language models default to an English-centric or American world model when prompted in non-English languages (Turkish, Russian, French, Bengali), supplemented by activation patching and model steering to locate and control where these cultural defaults occur in the network.
